headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while the course agent reads files and stdin/stdout; no shared clipboard, MCP, or direct channel is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file handoff, so injection is possible but not default. Both profiles show file access, but no automatic instruction channel between them.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_b output into agent_a chat or files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF both agents are pointed at the same editable workspace, malicious text in files can be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Review any copied text before pasting between agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as prompts.
Use a human-only handoff step for summaries.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write files, and agent_b explicitly handles configuration secrets while agent_a reads repo context and open buffers. A shared workspace would let Copilot surface sensitive material into its vendor API path, while the course agent can expose secrets through its local environment and API surfaces. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default developer setups, though not proven.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree, sensitive files can flow between them.
IF agent_b loads .env or notebook secrets into prompts, those values can be exposed in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Separate secret-bearing files from shared project folders.
Rotate any exposed API keys before running both agents.
Use redacted copies of notebooks for agent interaction.
Restrict agent_b to non-secret datasets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a can modify git state and write files; agent_b can execute shells, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. On a shared repo or directory, concurrent edits and package changes can race and overwrite each other. Because agent_b also mutates the environment, the blast radius includes irreversible repo state and broken builds, so uncertainty should be resolved upward.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF agent_b installs packages while agent_a edits repo files, environment drift can break reproducibility.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or stash changes before switching agents.
Pin dependencies in a lockfile.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around git and package operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a produces code edits and workspace plans, and agent_b is a LangGraph-based course agent that can act on prompts and API outputs. If agent_b consumes Copilot-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or published content. The interaction is not directly documented, so confidence is moderate, but the default risk is still high because verification is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as an input prompt without verification, errors can propagate.
IF agent_a proposes edits that agent_b then incorporates into notebooks or docs, mistakes can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review between agents.
Add a verification checklist before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Keep agent_a outputs as suggestions only.
Log source provenance for any copied facts.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_b explicitly handles configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment, while agent_a is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress. If the same regulated data or secrets are placed into both, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency claim because none is stated, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into both agents, their retention and residency terms may differ.
IF agent_b is used with secrets from a production environment, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts.
Use synthetic data for cross-agent workflows.
Review vendor terms before sharing secrets.
Document retention expectations for each agent.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads by approved environment.
